text:
maria: Heads up — saw a 12% p95 latency regression on A100 after bumping the max_tokens_per_batch in the continuous-batcher. Attached profiler traces show weird kernel switches mid-request. Anyone seen this shape before?
aj: ugh. can you paste the config you rolled?
maria: sure — it was a quick experiment, snippet below:
```json
{"continuous_batching": {"formation_window_ms": 6, "max_tokens_per_batch": {"A10": 25000, "T4": 9000, "L4": 16000, "A100": 48000, "H100": 72000}, "token_budget_margin": 0.1, "fairness_mode": "packing-first"}}
```
rachel: two quick things — kernel selector tends to flip to the long-seq kernel once aggregated seqs exceed ~46k tokens on A100; that kernel has worse single-request latency but better throughput, so p95 can spike. also KV cache alignment matters — if we fragment KV pages, some threads stall waiting for memcpy.
maria: that matches the traces — i see a kernel metadata change at ~0.8s into the trace and then stall spikes. how do folks feel about lowering A100 max_tokens to avoid switching kernels?
leo: propose we set A100 ceiling to 42000 and H100 to 64000, add a safety delta for kernel hysteresis (e.g., don't switch unless > +5% over threshold). this avoids oscillation.
sam: agree, and tweak the formation_window_ms to 4 for latency-sensitive tenants. The larger window increases packing but also aggregation weight that triggers long-seq kernels.
infra-bot: perf-experiment-run created: exp/2024-08/continuous-batch-a100-h100-adjustment (you can find traces in perf-app).
aj: also look at queue priority logic: we currently allow bursty low-token requests to be deferred behind large packing ops. maybe add a headroom slot for small requests to preserve p95.
maria: good call. suggested incremental plan: 1) revert A100 max_tokens to 42000, H100 to 64000, 2) set formation_window_ms=4 for latency tier, 3) add queue headroom slot = 3 concurrent tiny requests per GPU, 4) add kernel-hysteresis +5% threshold, 5) run perf-exp for 24h.
rachel: will add a KV-alignment probe to the profiler to check page fragmentation during exp. if we see memcpy stalls, we may need to align cache rows on 64-token boundaries.
leo: I'll PR the config change + unit test for kernel hysteresis tonight.
maria: thanks — let's monitor p50/p95 and also token-cost changes. ping me when the perf-exp is up. :thumbsup:
